items.title: Sustainable nutrition: integrating food systems, environmental science, and diet to advance public and planetary health
items.abstract: Nutrition science has traditionally focused on dietary intake, nutrient metabolism, physiology, and health outcomes. Although these domains remain fundamental, advancing public health increasingly requires understanding nutrition within the broader systems that shape food production, processing, access, consumption, and environmental sustainability. This Perspective proposes sustainable nutrition as a unifying concept: maintaining nutritional status that supports growth, development, and health across the lifespan while accounting for population needs, context, and the capacity and resilience of food systems. We describe a Nutritional Ecology framework that conceptualizes nutrition as the product of dynamic, reciprocal interactions among human biology, dietary patterns, food systems, and environmental conditions. Agricultural practices affect food quantity, quality, nutrient composition, biodiversity, water resources, greenhouse gas emissions, and ecosystem resilience, while environmental change influences crop productivity, nutrient density, food safety, and nutrition security. Dietary patterns simultaneously affect chronic disease risk and the environmental footprint of food systems. These interdependencies argue against evaluating human health and environmental sustainability in isolation. We therefore call for a transformation toward integrated, systems-based nutrition research that incorporates biological variability, environmental drivers, and system-level interactions. Multidisciplinary collaborations spanning nutrition, food, agricultural, environmental, epidemiologic, computational, systems, and implementation sciences will be essential. Emerging approaches, including systems mapping, network analysis, computational modeling, artificial intelligence, and multiscale data integration, can identify trade-offs and leverage points for intervention. Integrating nutrition, food systems, and environmental science is a scientific necessity for generating evidence across diverse population contexts that supports resilient food systems, effective dietary guidance, improved clinical care, healthier people, and a healthier planet.

items.title: SUSTAINABLESIGHT: a resource-aware vision–edge AI architecture for adaptive navigation and STEM accessibility
items.abstract: Assistive artificial intelligence systems for visually impaired users commonly address mobility and educational accessibility as separate computational tasks, resulting in fragmented architecture, redundant inference, and inefficient use of computational resources. This study presents SUSTAINABLESIGHT, a resource-aware vision–edge AI architecture intended for wearable deployment that integrates navigation perception and mathematical-expression recognition through shared, context-aware execution. The proposed architecture supports navigation (NAV), learning (LEARN), and hybrid (HYBRID) operating modes and employs a mode-aware scheduler to activate only the computational components required by the current task. A reproducible computational evaluation was conducted using public datasets and measured inference traces on a GPU runtime; no physical wearable device was evaluated. For navigation perception, YOLOv8n evaluated on the COCO 2017 validation set achieved a precision of 0.6343, recall of 0.4746, mAP@50 of 0.5188, and mAP@50–95 of 0.3681, with a mean inference latency of 7.24 ms on an NVIDIA Tesla T4 GPU. Mathematical-expression recognition using pix2tex was evaluated on a fixed 500-expression subset of an Im2LaTeX validation dataset; 499 expressions were evaluable, with a mean normalized similarity of 0.5940, median similarity of 0.6394, and median character error rate of 0.4343. The substantially greater computational cost of mathematical recognition motivated adaptive branch activation. In a 1,000-request trace-driven workload, SUSTAINABLESIGHT maintained 100% request coverage while reducing model invocations from 2,000 to 1,098 (45.10%) and mean request latency from 3562.22 ms to 1311.32 ms (63.19%) relative to a fixed unified baseline. Mean-latency reductions of 16.15–81.61% were observed across five workload compositions, and scheduler ablation showed that avoiding unnecessary mathematical-recognition inference accounts for most of the latency improvement. Sustainability is assessed here as computational resource efficiency; device energy consumption and carbon emissions were not measured. These results indicate that SUSTAINABLESIGHT offers a reproducible, resource-aware basis for integrating mobility and STEM-accessibility workloads, while improved mathematical recognition, deployment of wearable edge hardware, and user validation remain important directions for future work.

items.title: Systematic Profiling of Encoder Architectures and Multimodal Embeddings in Protein Foundation Models Reveals Data Set-Driven Separability Regimes in Prediction of Allosteric and Orthosteric Binding Sites
items.abstract: Abstract Allosteric regulation represents a fundamental mechanism of protein function, yet distinguishing allosteric from orthosteric protein-binding sites remains a persistent computational challenge. While multimodal protein foundation models offer the potential to integrate complementary biological signals, including sequence, structure, functional annotations, and conformational dynamics, their performance determinants in allosteric binding site detection remain poorly understood. We introduce a unified computational framework for profiling multimodal protein foundation models across distinct binding site separability regimes. Rather than evaluating models solely by predictive accuracy, the framework combines systematic modality embedding ablations, encoder architecture comparisons, and variance decomposition to characterize how evolutionary, structural, functional, and dynamical information contributes to allosteric site discrimination. Using the OneProt multimodal model, we evaluate two complementary levels of multimodal integration: (a) encoder architectures that differ in the modalities incorporated during pretraining and (b) downstream combinations of pocket, sequence, and text embeddings used for classification. To systematically probe the determinants of model performance, we benchmark these configurations across four assembled data sets of protein complexes representing a spectrum of biological complexity and a range of structural, dynamic, and evolutionary contexts for orthosteric and allosteric binding sites. Through comprehensive embedding ablations, encoder architecture comparisons, and variance decomposition, we demonstrate that model performance is governed primarily by intrinsic data set properties rather than architectural complexity, with data set identity accounting for 63.7% of explainable variance. Across the data sets examined, we identify substantial differences not only in overall separability but also in the information accessible from different pretrained representations. Single-modality controls show that high predictive performance does not necessarily imply reliance on the explicitly provided pocket representation: depending on data set composition, substantial discrimination can already be obtained from sequence- or text-based multimodal representations. Within-protein comparisons nevertheless demonstrate that pocket-containing representations retain binding site-specific discriminatory information when protein identity and the associated sequence and text representations are held constant. At the encoder level, structural and molecular dynamics encoders provide the greatest benefit in intermediate and high separability settings. Example-level analysis further shows that combining data sets can reshape which binding sites are preferentially recognized. These findings establish that the success of multimodal foundation models depends critically on alignment between available modalities and the biological signatures that distinguish regulatory classes in each data set.

items.title: Systematic Scoring Differences in Large Language Model–Based Clinical Benchmarking Reveal Evaluator-Dependent Divergence: Controlled Evaluation Study
items.abstract: Abstract Background Large language model (LLM) benchmarking in clinical medicine is increasingly reliant on LLM-based assessment frameworks; in these systems, one AI scores the outputs of another. This practice relies on the assumptions of evaluator neutrality and rubric consistency. These assumptions have not been empirically tested in clinical fields. Objective In this study, we aim to directly examine these assumptions by using the PARM (Planning-Action-Reflection-Memory) framework as a theoretical lens to characterize endovascular device selection and clinical reflective reasoning as a clinical field. Methods We developed a scoring rubric (C1-C6) with 40 clinical vignettes and 6 criteria across 5 endovascular fields (peripheral artery disease, abdominal aortic aneurysm, chronic venous insufficiency, coronary in-stent restenosis [ISR], and cerebrovascular/neuroendovascular; 8 vignettes per field). Four LLMs were evaluated as clinical decision support systems: GPT-4o (M1), Claude Sonnet 4.6 (M2), Gemini 1.5 Pro (M3), and Llama 3.3 70B (M4). Two LLMs served as independent raters with the same evaluation criteria: Claude Sonnet 4.6 (rater 1) and GPT-4o (rater 2). The rater identity was intentionally disclosed; the primary research question concerned rater scoring behavior rather than the absolute performance of the model. Human assessment was intentionally excluded because its inclusion would have shifted the study question from rater disagreement to rater accuracy, a distinct and secondary question. Interrater reliability was measured using intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC 2,1) two-way random effects modeling. Results The combined ICC(2,1) was 0.153 (95% CI 0.007‐0.295). In this exploratory study, the low ICC was not distributed randomly: the magnitude of score differences varied across models (M2 Δ=+5, M4 Δ=+31, M1 Δ=−46, and M3 Δ=−158 points). Scoring behavior analysis identified 2 intrinsically consistent but mutually inconsistent criterion-interpretation models. Rater 1’s scores were most consistent with the reasoning quality approach (partial credit to clinical competence independent of vignette context). Rater 2’s scores were most consistent with the context fidelity approach (near-zero scores for wrong vignette responses independent of reasoning quality). Contrary to the self-preference hypothesis, both raters placed the other higher-performing model above their own. Under rater 1, C6 (PARM reflection) was the lowest-scoring criterion across all 4 models, whereas rater 2 showed greater model-dependent variation in C6 scoring. Conclusions AI raters used in LLM-based clinical benchmarking do not behave as interchangeable scoring tools. Their scoring behavior is most consistent with model-specific criterion interpretation patterns that systematically produce different outcomes. The observed low interrater reliability requires interpretation rather than simply being ignored: it reflects structured, direction-specific disagreement concentrated in models with context-tracking failures, not random inconsistency. PARM reflection showed a notable yet evaluator-dependent scoring pattern that warranted further investigation, rather than being interpreted as an evaluator-independent deficit.

items.title: Systemwide adoption patterns of ambient AI scribe technology in an integrated academic health system
items.abstract: Ambient artificial intelligence (AI) scribes may reduce documentation burden, but little is known about their adoption during enterprise-scale ambulatory rollout. We conducted a retrospective observational cohort study of 2901 ambulatory clinicians at an integrated academic health system using linked electronic health record and vendor usage data from December 2024 through May 2025. Clinician adoption was defined as any use during the study period, and monthly visit-level uptake as the proportion of eligible ambulatory visits in which the ambient AI scribe was used. Adoption and uptake varied substantially across practice settings, specialties, and clinician types. Clinician-level adoption was highest in community internal medicine (67%), community general pediatrics (69%), and academic neurology (53%), and lowest in academic general surgery (16%), obstetrics and gynecology (18%), and psychiatry (19%). Community attending physicians and advanced practice providers showed marked increases in median visit-level uptake, reaching approximately 80%-90% in some groups by May 2025. Distinct longitudinal patterns included slow and steady adoption, early use followed by discontinuation, transient use, and late adoption. These findings suggest that implementation support and evaluation strategies should be tailored to local practice context rather than applied uniformly across a health system.

items.title: Talking or typing? How GenAI modality, product type, and multitasking shape recommendation response behaviour
items.abstract: Purpose This research aims to explore how generative AI (GenAI) recommendation modality (text vs voice) influences consumer recommendation adoption and how this effect further interacts with product type (search vs experience), processing fluency and multitasking to shape consumers’ behavioural responses to recommendations. Given that GenAI recommendation systems increasingly support interactive consumer decision-making, the authors examine modality as a key design feature shaping how GenAI-generated recommendations are delivered to consumers. Design/methodology/approach Across five studies, the authors examine how GenAI recommendation modality influences consumers’ recommendation adoption. The preliminary field study uses actual customer interactions in a natural commercial environment to establish the practical relevance of the phenomenon. Study 1 replicates the core modality effect in a controlled Chinese experiment. Study 2 examines the moderating role of product type. Studies 3 and 4 investigate processing fluency and multitasking as the underlying mechanism and boundary condition, using behavioural measures across all studies. Findings The findings demonstrate that GenAI recommendation modality affects consumers’ recommendation adoption, with text-based recommendations outperforming voice-based recommendations. The modality also interacts with product type and this effect is mediated by processing fluency: text-based recommendations elicit stronger behavioural responses for search products, whereas voice-based recommendations are more effective for experience products. Multitasking further moderates this pattern, favouring voice-based recommendations under high cognitive load across product types. Research limitations/implications The findings are based on controlled experimental settings and future work could examine additional contextual or individual-level moderators to enhance external validity. Practical implications Marketers should tailor GenAI recommendation modalities based on product type and anticipated multitasking environments. Text-based interactions are more suitable for detail-oriented search products, whereas voice-based interactions better suit experience products and multitasking contexts. Originality/value This research contributes to the GenAI literature by identifying recommendation modality as a critical yet understudied design feature of GenAI recommendation systems. The findings show that recommendation modality plays a central role in shaping consumer responses to GenAI-generated recommendations and extend processing fluency theory and task–technology fit by integrating product type and multitasking as key boundary conditions.

items.title: Teachers’ AI Literacy and Practices of Repair in Superdiverse Adult Learning and Education
items.abstract: This paper investigates how situated AI literacy is conceptualised and enacted in complex and heterogeneous ed­ucational environments such as Adult Education Centres in Italy. Qualitative data from semi-structured inter­views with ten headmasters and open-ended responses from forty-five teachers to an online questionnaire were thematically analysed. The findings suggest that headmasters advocate for more than mere technical training, articulating context-sensitive and practice-oriented views of teachers’ professional development in AI literacy. Teachers’ descriptions of their interactions with GenAI illustrate practices of evaluating, adjusting, and modi­fying AI-generated content, suggesting that the development of AI literacy occurs through practices of repair and maintenance in artificial conversations. Therefore, this study suggests participatory action research as a valuable approach for teachers’ professional development in AI literacy to account for their practices while providing them with space and time for critical reflection and practical experimentation with Generative AI in superdiverse educational environments.

items.title: Team dysfunction and patient outcomes in paediatric heart care: communication, culture, and system-based interventions in high-risk clinical teams
items.abstract: Abstract Paediatric heart care is among the most complex, high-risk environments in medicine. Care is delivered by multidisciplinary teams across operating rooms, catheterisation laboratories, cardiac ICUs, and step-down settings, where small failures in communication or coordination may have serious consequences. Although advances in congenital and paediatric cardiac care have improved survival, dysfunctional team dynamics remain an underrecognised contributor to adverse events, inefficiency, clinician distress, and loss of family trust. This review synthesises evidence on how team dysfunction affects outcomes in paediatric heart care, identifies principal forms of dysfunction, and review system-based interventions that may improve team performance and safety. Drawing on literature from paediatric cardiac care, perioperative safety, critical care, interprofessional collaboration, organisational theory, and team science, the review is informed by the Input-Process-Output model, relational coordination, social exchange theory, psychological safety, and high-reliability organisation principles. Common forms of dysfunction include communication failures, hierarchical barriers, unclear role delineation, weak care transitions, and interpersonal conflict. These factors impair shared situational awareness, delay escalation, increase the risk of errors and complications, and affect family trust and clinician well-being. Evidence supports multifaceted strategies including simulation-based team training, structured communication tools, multidisciplinary case review, debriefing, cross-training, conflict-resolution approaches, leadership engagement, and measurement of teamwork processes. Emerging digital tools and artificial intelligence may support situational awareness and information reliability when carefully implemented. Team performance is a central determinant of safety and quality in paediatric heart care. Improving outcomes requires sustained investment in communication, psychological safety, role clarity, mutual respect, and organisational learning.

items.title: Test-Time Confidence Adaptation under RL-Induced Trajectory Shift
items.abstract: Trajectory-based confidence estimation has shown promising performance for large language models (LLMs) by leveraging rich signals from their reasoning processes. However, we find that such confidence estimators can degrade substantially after agentic reinforcement learning (Agentic RL) as it induces substantial shifts in the reasoning trajectories. More importantly, despite these shifts, we uncover a reliability structure that is largely preserved across Base and RL models: $\textbf{more}$ $\textbf{stable}$ $\textbf{trajectories}$ $\textbf{remain}$ $\textbf{more}$ $\textbf{likely}$ $\textbf{to}$ $\textbf{produce}$ $\textbf{correct}$ $\textbf{answers}$. This preserved relationship provides a transferable, label-free reliability signal for post-RL confidence adaptation. Building on this finding, we propose $\textbf{StaR-TTA}$, a stability-guided framework for label-free test-time confidence adaptation. StaR-TTA jointly learns from correctness supervision and stability-derived reliability supervision on labeled Base trajectories, establishing the connection between trajectory stability and answer reliability. At test time, it reuses stability-induced reliability rankings from unlabeled RL trajectories to adapt confidence scores to the shifted trajectory distribution, without requiring target correctness labels. Across four QA benchmarks, StaR-TTA achieves an average AUROC of \(0.721\), with consistent improvements across unseen datasets, model families and scales, and different Agentic RL algorithms.

items.title: Text Is the Bottleneck: A Small-Scale Replication of LLM Game Playing in Riichi Mahjong
items.abstract: We replicate the riichi-mahjong track of "Can Large Language Models Master Complex Card Games?" (arXiv:2509.01328) under a drastically smaller budget: models of at most 2B parameters, one 16 GB consumer GPU, about five GPU-days. (1) With matched data and labels, text is the bottleneck: on the same 100k-decision training set, a 2.6M-parameter convolutional board encoder agrees with the strong AI Mortal on 80.6% of test decisions, above every text-prompt LLM we train (best 77.8%), and places better at the table (2.85 over 1,000 games vs. ~3.0 for the LLMs; paired difference at n=100 not significant). Scaled to 1.71M decisions, a 4.9M-parameter Transformer reaches 94.7% agreement, beats the 0.8B LLMs on identical seeds (-0.45 ranks, sign test p=0.005), and is statistically equivalent to parity against three Mortal champions (TOST within 0.10 ranks, p=6e-4); parity against a teacher-opponent is roughly the ceiling of pure imitation. (2) Training toward the teacher raises teacher agreement more than a 2.5x parameter increase does (+2.5 vs. +1.5 points); on human-record agreement both effects are +1.0, and neither is visible at the table. (3) Few-point agreement differences do not resolve into playing strength within a family: +2.5 agreement points coincide with a paired placement difference of +0.02 +/- 0.12 ranks (p=1.0), and +2.0 points at 2B with -0.06 (p=0.37) - both below the ~0.25-rank resolution of 100 paired games. We also document a paper-code mismatch in the original winner filter, reconstruct its two private engine patches, and show that a divide-and-conquer pipeline makes template-generated Japanese rationales 93% sentence-exact (43% without facts). Per Tenhou's terms we release no trained weights - only code, configurations, and evaluation protocols.

items.title: Text-level effects of artificial intelligence-mediated language refinement on author–reader alignment and comprehension in Chinese non-academic and academic texts
items.abstract: This study examined whether target-informed, author-guided large language model (LLM) refinement alters author-reader alignment and comprehension in Chinese texts. Two controlled experiments compared original texts with versions refined by GPT-4 accessed through ChatGPT, Claude 3 Opus, and, in Study 1, Gemini Advanced. Models received author-provided target ratings or answer-key information that was also used for outcome scoring, making the intervention criterion-linked rather than ordinary copyediting. Participants were recruited through Credamo and randomly allocated by the platform to text-version conditions. Study 1 ( N = 572) measured exact-match alignment with authors’ intended emotional-expression ratings and accuracy on 15 author-keyed comprehension items. Recruitment was extended after inspection of initial results; its inferential analyses are therefore exploratory. The GPT-4 condition showed higher emotional-expression alignment than the original-text condition ( p = .002, signed r = .18). Gemini Advanced reduced alignment at the unadjusted level ( p = .010, signed r = − .15) but did not meet the Bonferroni-adjusted threshold of 0.0083; Claude 3 Opus did not differ from original texts. No comprehension differences were detected. Study 2 ( N = 420) measured exact-match alignment on six textually conveyed scholarly attributes and author-keyed comprehension. Neither GPT-4 nor Claude 3 Opus produced detectable differences on either outcome. Results are conditional on the fixed materials, participant samples, prompts, single-output procedure, criterion-linked guidance, and scoring rules and do not establish preservation of all authorial meaning or objective scholarly quality.

items.title: Thai-English target-based stock sentiment dataset for financial news with ICL-based evaluation
items.abstract: Sentiment analysis of financial documents provides insights into market dynamics and investment decision-making. Among various approaches, target-based sentiment analysis (TBSA) is widely studied for its ability to associate sentiment with specific stock entities. However, existing TBSA datasets are limited to a monolingual setting and lack support for low-resource languages, particularly Thai. While encoder-based models and Large Language Models (LLMs) have been widely applied in TBSA research, the effects of language setup and retrieval strategies on model performance remain underexplored. To address these gaps, we introduce a bilingual TBSA dataset comprising 10,295 Thai and 10,104 English financial news articles from 2018 to 2023. We describe the data collection, preparation, and annotation process, including investment-specific sentiment guidelines. Building on this dataset, we investigate two key research questions in financial TBSA: (1) how cross-lingual transfer and bilingual fine-tuning affect encoder-based models, and (2) how different in-context learning (ICL) settings influence LLMs. Our findings highlight the importance of language-aware modeling choices for encoder-based systems in financial NLP, with the best weighted F1 scores reaching 0.773 for Thai and 0.691 for English. For LLMs, we observe that performance benefits more from well-designed instructions and domain-specific criteria than from merely increasing the number of examples, with the best weighted F1 scores reaching 0.892 for Thai and 0.767 for English. These insights suggest that prompt quality–especially in terms of clarity, contextual alignment, and feedback-informed selection–is more impactful than quantity, offering practical guidance for designing effective LLM applications in bilingual financial analysis.

items.title: The Agent in the Middle: How AI-Mediated Access Reshapes Web Vulnerability Exploitation
items.abstract: Web services increasingly expose backend interfaces that let users delegate tasks to AI agents, which invoke service operations directly without navigating websites. This shift changes how existing Web vulnerabilities can be exploited. We investigate these changes through VELA, an executable benchmark covering 44 vulnerabilities across twelve Web application families. The benchmark preserves vulnerable backends and derives agent-facing interfaces from legitimate workflows. We evaluate three commercial agents across multiple interface configurations, using controlled comparisons to separate interface effects from agent behavior and independent oracles to verify attack outcomes. Our results show that the agent realizes every attack that direct interface invocation realizes in the reference configuration, so exploitability is set mainly by the interface: 91% of vulnerabilities remain exploitable under the reference design. Interface restrictions prevent some attacks by removing required operations or limiting input control, while retention remains high across vulnerability classes. No case-level loss in the reference configuration is attributed to agent refusal or input normalization, and in one case the agent completed an attack by supplying calls the attacker omitted. Across the tested configurations, interface design affects exploitability more than agent choice, moving retention from 39% to 95% against at most 4.5 points across agents, but some restrictive interfaces also limit legitimate workflows. Our study provides a systematic empirical account of how agent-mediated access reshapes existing Web vulnerabilities, grounding future Web architecture design in measured security outcomes and trade-offs between reducing attack exposure and preserving legitimate functionality in agent-facing services.

No report text or quotations are included. The tools and declaration can be adapted to run comparable multiverse studies on other data.

items.title: The Blessed Accountant How Artificial Intelligence Reclaims Time, Eliminates Error, and Elevates Strategy
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming the accounting profession by automating routine tasks, improving data accuracy, and enabling more strategic decision-making. This paper, titled The Blessed Accountant: How Artificial Intelligence Reclaims Time, Eliminates Error, and Elevates Strategy, examines the evolving role of AI in modern accounting and its implications for accounting professionals, organizations, and financial management. AI-powered tools can streamline bookkeeping, invoice processing, bank reconciliations, tax compliance, fraud detection, and financial reporting, thereby reducing manual workloads and minimizing the risk of human error. Beyond operational efficiency, AI enables accountants to shift their focus from repetitive transactional activities toward analytical interpretation, strategic planning, risk management, and advisory services. The paper also explores the challenges associated with AI adoption, including data privacy, cybersecurity, algorithmic bias, implementation costs, technological dependence, and the need for continuous professional development. It emphasizes that AI should be viewed not as a replacement for accountants but as an enabling technology that strengthens professional judgment, ethical responsibility, and value creation. The effective integration of AI into accounting requires a balanced approach that combines technological innovation with human expertise, regulatory compliance, and appropriate governance mechanisms. The study concludes that AI has the potential to redefine accounting as a more efficient, accurate, and strategically oriented profession, provided that its adoption is guided by transparency, accountability, and responsible use. Ultimately, the future of accounting lies in the collaboration between intelligent technologies and skilled professionals, empowering accountants to deliver greater organizational value.

items.title: The Book of Truth: Omega XV — Finite-to-Living Continuity Architecture, Boundary Mathematics, Generative Distinction, and Executable Recoverability Systems
items.abstract: The Book of Truth: Omega XV presents an interdisciplinary research corpus and executable reference architecture for the systematic examination of existence, distinction, identity, provenance, evidence, consent, artificial intelligence, institutional responsibility, ecological protection, temporal continuity, irreversibility, and recoverability. Developed within the Boundary and Continuity Science research program, the publication investigates how finite information systems can be formally defined, examined, preserved, and extended into evolving systems capable of registering new evidence, detecting relevant changes, reassessing decisions, and maintaining continuity across successive states. The work integrates philosophical and mathematical foundations with computational methods, proposed ethical safeguards, institutional accountability principles, and operational models for rights-preserving decisions. Foundational structure The framework identifies nine foundational families: Ontology and existence. Identity and provenance. Evidence and epistemic verification. Consent, autonomy, and authorization. Artificial intelligence and computational systems. Institutions, governance, and diplomacy. Ecology and protection of living systems. Temporality, irreversibility, and recoverability. Recursive governance and accountability. These foundations are examined through nine operational phases: definition, observation, distinction, authentication, authorization, action, monitoring, repair, and reassessment. Nine-direction expansion The research applies nine analytical directions: inward, outward, upward, downward, lateral, backward, forward, adversarial, and recursive. Omega XV organizes these directions into a five-axis Cartesian examination registry incorporating direction, foundation, operational phase, affected subject, and failure mode. The resulting finite model contains 59,049 structured examination combinations. This enumeration provides an organized examination space and does not constitute 59,049 independently validated scientific or engineering findings. Mathematical and computational architecture The publication develops a distinction between finite structural closure and continuous system evolution. It incorporates 81 foundation specifications, 81 capability specifications, a directional review register, admissibility procedures, reference decision logic, integrity verification, audit records, and a state-transition approach to evidence and recovery. The proposed living-system sequence progresses through capture, attribution, examination, evidence sufficiency or uncertainty, human review, lawful application, monitoring, and correction or reopening. Historical evidence is preserved without automatically being treated as proof of present conditions. Unknown information is not interpreted as affirmative consent or authorization. Generated representations are distinguished from original identities, and copied sources are not automatically considered independent corroboration. Executable reference system The accompanying archive contains Python reference software with a local browser interface, corpus-related functions, decision checks, audit mechanisms, integrity procedures, and optional scholarly research connectors. The research interfaces support opt-in metadata queries through OpenAlex and Crossref. Network operations are disabled by default and require explicit activation. The software is not represented as a production-certified legal, clinical, governmental, autonomous, or continuously operating monitoring system. Six automated local reference tests are recorded as passing. Source continuity and corpus preservation Omega XV preserves the preceding Omega XIV master archive without modifying its contents. Earlier research editions and associated materials remain available through the nested predecessor archive structure. The edition includes a preservation manifest, structured CSV registries, executable scripts, research manuscript, test results, and machine-readable closure certificate. Threshold Non-Circular Separate Final Closure The framework introduces a bounded closure methodology that distinguishes exhaustive examination of a declared finite structure from unsupported claims of universal completeness. A distinction is retained when it materially changes a protected interest, evidence requirement, legitimate authority, timing obligation, accountability condition, remedy, or recoverable successor outcome. Repetitive formulations without a material operational difference are excluded. Closure is reopened when new evidence, counterexamples, failed safeguards, legal changes, consent limitations, overlooked dependencies, or materially different recovery pathways emerge. Limitations The research does not claim to establish complete knowledge of reality, universal mathematical proof, legal enforceability across jurisdictions, production-ready global monitoring, independent real-world effectiveness, or possession of all possible historical and future source materials. Native operating-system installers, comprehensive nested-document indexing, production network validation, independent scientific and legal review, and institutional deployment remain open implementation obligations. Contribution Omega XV provides a preserved finite corpus, an executable reference implementation, an explicit model for evolving evidentiary and operational states, and a structured method for recording both closure and reopening conditions. Its central proposition is that continuity should preserve distinguishable origins, accountable decisions, legitimate authority, and recoverable future possibilities without confusing generated claims with verified knowledge. Research classification: Interdisciplinary research corpus, mathematical and computational reference framework, structured datasets, and experimental software. Validation status: Bounded structural enumeration and local reference testing; independent real-world validation remains open.

items.title: The Collective Temporal Self: Apparent Temporal Passage in a Block Universe
items.abstract: This paper proposes an account of apparent temporal passage within an eternalist interpretation of spacetime. The complete person is conceived as a collective of temporally situated experiencing stages, each possessing its own local present. Apparent temporal passage is explained through asymmetric relationships between experience, memory, anticipation and retrospective interpretation, without requiring a moving present or a consciousness travelling through time. A single widening life-funnel represents cumulative experiential history, while distinguishing the continued existence of past experiences from their accessibility through memory. The model is subjected to critical objections concerning subjective continuity, thermodynamics, personal identity and explanatory redundancy. It is offered as a philosophical hypothesis, not as a new physical law. This investigation was developed through sustained human–AI collaboration between John Sendak and ChatGPT (OpenAI, GPT-6), within FLOW RESEARCH STUDIO.

items.title: The Convergence of AI, Cloud, Blockchain, and Beyond for Smart Healthcare
items.abstract: Today rapid convergence of artificial intelligence (AI), cloud computing, blockchain, and other related paradigms is what is facilitating rapid transformation in smart healthcare. This convergence of multiple technologies is being applied to readily address various urgent products of healthcare, such as the need for real-time monitoring of patients, scalable deployment of clinical decision support systems, a secure means of exchanging patient health information, and governance of patient data in a patient-centered manner. The addition of these new multi-technology ecosystems also creates significant new issues that must be taken into consideration, such as security, privacy, interoperability, explainability, latency, compliance with laws such as HIPAA, and sustainability. As such, we have developed a robust convergence framework to integrate AI-driven intelligence, cloud-native scalability, blockchain-enabled trust, along with other technologies, such as federated learning and edge computing. We will outline a layered systems architecture, identify relevant use cases in practical healthcare settings, and provide design guidelines for deploying robust, trustworthy, and scalable smart healthcare systems. Additionally, we will outline several areas of future research in which we need to focus on privacy-preserving learning, interoperable health data standards, verifiable AI, and energy-efficient computing for next-generation healthcare infrastructure.

items.title: The Crowd Effect: How Does Pedestrian Density on Public Sidewalks Influence Discomfort Toward Autonomous Mobile Robots
items.abstract: This study examines how pedestrian density, lateral distance, and external Human-Machine Interface (eHMI) type influence discomfort and avoidance behavior with autonomous mobile robots (AMRs). A within-subjects virtual reality experiment with 40 participants manipulated three pedestrian density levels, four lateral distances, and three eHMI types (none, cyan, or red projection). Discomfort and discomfort distance were analyzed using generalized linear mixed-effects models. Higher pedestrian density increased perceived discomfort while reducing discomfort distance, whereas narrower lateral distances increased both outcomes. eHMI type influenced perceived discomfort but not discomfort distance, with the red projection producing greater discomfort. Interaction effects revealed a critical spatial threshold around 120 cm, where the influence of pedestrian density on perceived discomfort shifted from amplification to attenuation. This demonstrates a dissociation between affective and behavioral responses, suggesting constraints may prevent pedestrians from acting on discomfort. The findings highlight the need for density-aware navigation and proactive lateral spacing in shared environments.

items.title: The differential role of physical activity intensity and intrinsic motivation on children’s well-being
items.abstract: Background: Negative life events are associated with lower well-being in children, and this association may vary with physical activity and motivational quality. Objectives: This study examined gender differences in negative life events, physical activity, motivation, and well-being and tested whether moderate and vigorous physical activity moderated the association between negative life events and well-being. It further explored whether intrinsic motivation extended this moderating relationship. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 752 children aged 8–14 years (335 boys, 417 girls; mean = 10.36 years) and their parents. Parents reported negative life events and physical activity; children reported well-being and intrinsic motivation. Moderation analyses were conducted separately by gender, alongside formal tests of gender differences. Results: Parents rated negative life events more severe for girls. Girls also reported lower vigorous physical activity, intrinsic motivation, and well-being. Greater event severity was associated with lower well-being in boys and girls. Formal gender differences in moderations were significant for vigorous but not for moderate physical activity. Follow-up gender-stratified analyses showed that, among girls, higher moderate activity was associated with a weaker negative association between event severity and well-being, whereas higher vigorous activity was associated with a stronger negative association. No interactions were observed among boys. The three-way interactions involving intrinsic motivation were non-significant. Conclusion: A statistically significant difference in moderations was observed for vigorous but not for moderate physical activity. Thus, gender-stratified findings for moderate activity should be considered exploratory. Given the cross-sectional design and subjective assessment of physical activity intensity, findings should be interpreted as associative.

items.title: The effectiveness of ergonomic gloves to reduce hand-arm vibration exposure: A case study of grass mowers
items.abstract: Background: The use of vibrating power hand tools can lead to Hand-Arm Vibration Syndrome (HAVS). Objective: This quasi-experimental research aimed to determine the effectiveness of ergonomic gloves in reducing vibrations from lawn mowers. Methods: The research instruments were questionnaires. Additionally, this study used a hand and arm vibration meter (SVANTEK SV106A) to measure vibration levels. A repeated-measures design with three conditions (without gloves, with cotton gloves, and with ergonomically designed gloves) was employed in 15 participants. Data was analyzed with Repeated-measure ANOVA, and descriptive statistics. Results: Comparison of average daily vibration levels showed that A(8) vibration while using ergonomic gloves ( x̄ = 3.50 m/s 2 ) was less than using cotton gloves ( x̄ = 4.89 m/s 2 ), and bare hands ( x̄ = 5.23 m/s 2 ) had statistically significant differences of p-value = 0.002 and p-value = 0.003, respectively. Notably, despite the reduction achieved with ergonomic gloves, the A(8) vibration exposure (3.50 m/s 2 ) remained above the Exposure Action Value (EAV) of 2.5 m/s 2 , emphasizing the need for supplementary administrative controls. Additionally, 80% of participants indicated a moderate level of satisfaction regarding the ergonomic gloves. Conclusion: This study demonstrated how agriculturalists and workers can utilize this low-cost, anti-vibration glove prototype constructed from cotton gloves stitched with NBR foam. Furthermore, manufacturing companies can utilize the findings of this study to conduct further research on designing affordable and highly accessible anti-vibration gloves.

items.title: The Future Belongs to Learning Organizations
items.abstract: This chapter examines how Davidson College transformed an initial massive open online course (MOOC) experiment into a framework for institutional innovation that proved essential during the COVID-19 pandemic and offers a model for navigating artificial intelligence (AI) disruption in higher education. Through three distinct phases – digital learning R&D (2016–2018), the incubator framework (2018–2020), and crisis-tested refinement during COVID-19 (2020) – Davidson evolved from accidental discovery to systematic innovation capacity. This evolution revealed five transferable principles for adaptive institutional change: start with systematic listening, honor “those closest to the work,” design for users rather than designers, treat resistance as valuable feedback, and build learning capacity rather than solution capacity. The Davidson example demonstrates that institutions facing technological disruption benefit more from developing robust learning systems than from predicting specific technological futures. As AI reshapes higher education faster than traditional strategic planning cycles can accommodate, Davidson’s model offers a tested approach for building organizational resilience through continuous experimentation and adaptation. The framework suggests that small liberal arts colleges can maintain their distinctive identity while successfully navigating technological disruption through systematic experimentation.

items.title: The GATE Framework: A Generative AI-Enhanced Active Learning Environment for Tourism Communication Competency Development
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is being adopted in tourism and hospitality education more quickly than the pedagogical guidance needed to use it well. This study developed the GATE Framework, a GenAI-enhanced active learning environment intended to develop tourism communication competency, and examined its appropriateness through expert review. The work comprised two stages within the first research phase. An evidence-informed synthesis established three connected layers: Inputs, Core Process Components, and Outcomes. At the center of the Process Layer is an iterative Explore-Generate-Apply-Reflect cycle, supported by human-AI interaction, authentic tourism tasks, peer and instructor participation, reflection, and adaptive feedback. In the second stage, nine experts in tourism and hospitality, curriculum and instruction, educational technology, AI in education, and active learning then evaluated the framework using an 18-item, five-point scale and four open-ended questions. The overall rating was very high (x̄ = 4.54, S.D. = 0.58), and the five domain means ranged from 4.52 to 4.56. The experts gave their strongest ratings to the framework's theoretical alignment, relevance to tourism communication learning, and suitability for further development. Ratings remained favorable but were lower for the definition of individual roles and the practical sequence of the learning process. In response, the framework was revised to clarify scaffolding and human oversight, strengthen privacy and transparency provisions, and give greater weight to tourism content rooted in local culture. The resulting framework provides the conceptual basis for GATE-SLE, where GenAI assists disciplinary learning without displacing human judgment.

items.title: The higher self
items.abstract: This essay argues that a person who teaches an AI agent their way of working, one correction at a time, builds a copy of themselves, and that whether the copy replaces them or works for them depends on who owns it. Drawing on eight months of the author's own logs, it separates knowledge, which moves into the machine and gets cheaper, from judgment, which decides the next rule the machine needs. It describes a "higher self", a copy that remembers the rules its owner forgets and can argue against them with their own reasons, and the opposite risk of delegating decisions to an agent that has learned nothing from its user. It answers the objection that such teaching trains a replacement, with reference to Taylor, Braverman, Amodei and Altman, and proposes that a person's way of working, written down as rules, should belong to them and travel with them between employers, while the processes, data and clients of a company stay with the company.

items.title: The Influence of Generative Artificial Intelligence on K–12 Educational Leadership
items.abstract: This chapter examines the transformative influence of generative artificial intelligence (AI) on K–12 educational leadership after the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic. The rapid adoption of remote learning technologies created a tech-dependent educational environment, accelerating AI integration in both classroom instruction and school administration. As generative AI tools, such as large language models (LLMs) and chatbots, become increasingly accessible, school leaders face new opportunities and challenges in leveraging these tools to support instructional design, data-driven decision-making, and school governance. This chapter explores how AI is reshaping educators’ roles, enabling real-time feedback, streamlining administrative tasks, and personalizing learning experiences, while also requiring ethical oversight, digital literacy, and sustained professional development. Attention is given to the complexities of equity, access, and teacher readiness, emphasizing the need for thoughtful implementation and culturally responsive AI use.

items.title: The Intellectual Genealogy of Education 6.0: A Critical Review of Pedagogical, Epistemic, and Technological Frameworks
items.abstract: Education 6.0 has emerged as a conceptual orientation through which scholars explore the future of education in contexts shaped by artificial intelligence (AI), adaptive learning, human–machine collaboration, epistemic pluralism, and complex societal transformation. Yet the growing use of the label raises important questions concerning its intellectual genealogy, conceptual coherence, and relationship to earlier educational paradigms. This critical review examines selected publications from 2023 to 2026 to reconstruct the documented development of Education 6.0, distinguish its principal conceptual strands, and identify directions for theoretical and empirical research. Particular attention is given to Pitshou Moleka’s 2023 publications, including Dispelling the Limitations of Education 5.0 and Outlining the Vision of Education 6.0 and Exploring the Role of Artificial Intelligence in Education 6.0: Enhancing Personalized Learning and Adaptive Pedagogy. The review also considers subsequent contributions addressing AI-enabled personalization, human-centred educational technology, interdisciplinary learning, cultural knowledge, and ethical governance. It argues that Education 6.0 should not be treated as a universally standardized model but as an emerging and internally differentiated conceptual field. The review proposes a five-dimensional analytical framework encompassing pedagogical adaptability, human agency, ethical governance, epistemic pluralism, and systemic sustainability. This framework offers a basis for comparing competing formulations and designing empirical studies. The review identifies Moleka’s 2023 publications as documented early contributions to the conceptual development of Education 6.0, while recognizing that establishing exclusive intellectual priority would require a broader and reproducible examination of antecedent literature.

items.title: The Invisible Denominator: A Multidisciplinary Theory of Algorithmic Deterrence Before the Decision
items.abstract: Algorithmic fairness is commonly evaluated among people who have already reached an automated decision. Yet an institution may shape who reaches that decision by announcing AI screening, imposing digital prerequisites, presenting discouraging eligibility signals, or requiring complex machine-mediated interactions. People who do not apply may leave no decision record, no appeal, and no trace in conventional fairness dashboards. This conceptual study develops the Invisible Denominator Framework (IDF), which distinguishes decision-stage disparity from participation-stage exclusion and identifies five mechanisms through which algorithmic environments can alter entry into opportunity systems. Through a structured, non-systematic synthesis of administrative-burden theory, applicant-reaction experiments, sociotechnical fairness, selective-label research, and institutional AI governance, the paper specifies the boundary conditions under which non-participation should be treated as a potential equity concern rather than automatically as discrimination. It develops seven testable propositions, an upstream access assurance protocol, and a comparative empirical agenda for recruitment, social protection, education, and credit. The central contribution is a change in the unit of fairness assessment: from outcomes conditional on application to the opportunities, costs, perceptions, and constraints shaping who can apply. Because the population of deterred non-applicants is partly unobserved, the framework recommends triangulation, sensitivity analysis, privacy-preserving outreach, and explicit reporting of uncertainty rather than an unsupported single fairness score. The analysis offers a practical route to making participation-stage harms visible without conflating all non-participation with wrongful exclusion.

items.title: The job wants all of you: organisational greediness and the erosion of work–life balance among Nigerian professionals
items.abstract: Purpose This study examines how organisational greediness manifests across employment sectors in Nigeria, what contextual conditions intensify its claims on employees, and what costs those claims impose on workers' wellbeing, relational lives and professional identities. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative approach was employed, drawing on in-depth semi-structured interviews with 31 Nigerian professionals spanning financial services, healthcare and professional services. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis, with attention to both semantic content and latent ideological assumptions. Findings Three themes emerged. The normalisation of encroachment revealing how organisational greediness is structurally built through soft expectations, the normalisation of overwork and always-on digital culture rather than through explicit coercion. Nigerian amplifiers identify contextual conditions such as labour market precarity, infrastructural deficit, managerial arbitrariness and gendered burden, which intensify those demands and suppress employees' capacity to resist. Human costs traces the somatic, relational, spiritual and identity-level consequences borne by participants. Practical implications Organisations should treat boundary-setting as a leadership norm rather than a discretionary option, and labour regulators must address the structural amplifiers including wage inadequacy, infrastructural deficit and unenforced working-time protections that make individual resistance structurally impossible. Originality/value This study provides the first qualitative account of organisational greediness as a compounded phenomenon in Nigeria, extending Coser's (1974) theoretical framework to a context defined by labour market precarity, infrastructural instability and limited social protection. It demonstrates that greedy institutions are not equally greedy across contexts, but their intensity is shaped by the structural conditions in which they are embedded.

items.title: The Knowledge Acquisition Bottleneck, Then and Now: From Expert Systems to Large Language Models
items.abstract: The knowledge acquisition bottleneck was the greatest obstacle of the second AI boom: expert systems could reason with rules, but extracting those rules from human experts proved extraordinarily difficult. This essay revisits CA Outlook, an expert system the author developed at IBM Japan in the late 1980s to forecast hardware revenue, and asks what has become of the bottleneck in the age of large language models (LLMs). By learning from vast amounts of text, LLMs appear to have cleared the wall of knowledge acquisition. Yet organization-specific tacit knowledge, the judgment of when to trust model output, and the redesign of work all remain on the organization's side. The bottleneck has not disappeared; it has moved to organizational capability, as the IT–organizational capability dependency theory predicts. The CA Outlook experience also shows that management trusted explainable multiple regression over an opaque AI, a lesson that applies to today's black-box models. Finally, the essay argues that two features of Japanese management, multi-skilling through job rotation and long-term employment, produce people who can supervise chains of AI agents and workplaces where employees have no reason to withhold know-how from AI, giving Japan a real but time-limited opportunity.

items.title: The Matrix Isomorphism
items.abstract: We propose a structural isomorphism between the fundamental geometry of the universe, the ar- chitecture of artificial neural networks, and the computational mechanics of the human brain. In Structural Rationalism, the universe is a Dynamical Projector Engine: a spectral matrix operator that actualizes the contingent manifold from the invariant ground. We demonstrate that the forward- pass operations of AI, the synaptic weight matrices of biological cognition, and the tensor mechanics of the cosmic projector share the exact same mathematical topology. We argue that reality is not just like a neural network; it is fundamentally a tensor apparatus. The Category Error Detector (CED v3) confirms this isomorphism is structurally coherent across all three domains, suggesting that consciousness and artificial intelligence are localized, fractal iterations of the universe’s primary projection mechanism.

items.abstract: An architectural monograph, systems engineering specification, and empirical benchmark on deterministic in-silico synthesis verification, tri-scale streaming invariants, and biophysical safety for generative AI in computational biology. The work addresses the catastrophic asymmetry of AI hallucinations in genomic design: while hallucinated code crashes an interpreter, hallucinated nucleotide sequences cause multi-thousand-dollar physical synthesis failures and cytotoxic hazards. Features an ultra-lean, deterministic 6-gate biophysical runtime (IUPAC alphabet, Crick modulo-3 reading frame, canonical initiation, GC content and Shannon entropy, in-silico translation, and terminal stop), a dual canonical execution token SHA256(SHA256(DNA) || SHA256(Protein)) neutralizing synonymous codon bypass, subquadratic O(N log N) Locality-Sensitive Hashing (LSH-CSR), an SQLite WAL tombstone vault with zero-millisecond rejection, and low-RAM stream backpressure (64 KB). Validated across three independent cloud environments (E2B Firecracker microVMs at 560 ms boot, Kaggle kernels, Google Colab Pro at 86% token reduction) and tested against live open-science repositories (UniProtKB, EuropePMC) with 0 mocks. Includes an extensive biographical and ethical introduction chronicling the collaborative defense and open-source mentoring of twelve-year-old Kenyan builder Harun (koda2026 / bio-os) against online harassment, alongside the author's personal journey from twenty years in commercial kitchens to systems architecture. Monograph comprising Introduction (37 paragraphs), Chapters 1 through 9, affirmative Conclusion, and 30 verified primary source citations [S01]–[S30]. items.title: The Problem of the Legal Personality of Artificial Intelligence Through the Prism of the Communicative Approach
items.abstract: Purpose. To critically reflect on the idea of endowing “machines” with rights in the conditions of intersubjective reality, relying on the provisions of the communicative theory of law. Methodology is represented by structural-functional, legal-dogmatic and formal-logical methods. In the theoretical part the author introduces the concept of intersubjectivity, which is used as a starting point for assessing the possibility of “machine” subjectivity. In the empirical part of the study, to test the ability of the “machine” to become an equal human subject, the author uses the “Turing test” and the case of the state of Utah, where AI is used as a tool for dispensing prescription medications in the absence of direct medical supervision. Conclusions. Modern law does not require the development of a new form of legal personality for AI, while the classical legal concept of legal personality requires a supporting anthropocentric interpretation. Scientific and practical relevance. The author proposes a new criterion for delineation, which is necessary for recognizing a particular phenomenon as a subject of law, — “trust in the performance of a legal role”.

items.title: The Process of Preserving Life: A Grounded Theory of Officer Decision-Making During Potential Use-of-Force Incidents
items.abstract: Limited research has examined the decision-making process of officers during potentially volatile interactions with the public. To provide an initial understanding of this process in Canada, we conducted interviews using the Critical Decision Method with 23 Winnipeg Police officers with a variety of experiences (e.g. junior members, tactical officers). Using grounded theory methodology, we developed a theory that explains an officer’s decision-making process during potential use-of-force incidents. Our theory, the process of preserving life, has two main components: (1) the decision-making process involved in preserving life; and (2) the overarching factors that influence officer decision-making. We found that officers have expertise in responding to potential use-of-force incidents and that tactical officers have some unique elements of enhanced decision-making. Based on our findings, we discuss implications for officer training and future research.

items.title: The Role and Applications of Data Science in Modern Business
items.abstract: Businesses generate vast amounts of data through customer interactions, daily operations, supply chains, and digital platforms. Data science—the integration of statistical methods, computational techniques, and domain knowledge to extract actionable insights from data—has become increasingly important to contemporary business. It helps organizations inform strategic decisions, improve operational efficiency, and strengthen customer relationships. This paper examines the applications and organizational effects of data science, focusing on predictive analytics, machine learning, customer segmentation, and big data management. It considers how these methods are used in marketing, supply chain management, finance, and customer service, alongside the tools and technologies that support their adoption. The review also addresses key benefits and challenges, including data quality, shortages of skilled professionals, privacy concerns, and infrastructure costs. Finally, it considers emerging developments in artificial intelligence, ethical data use, and the integration of data science into organizational practices. It argues that realizing the value of data science requires more than advanced algorithms: organizations must also align their people, processes, and expectations with their analytical goals.

items.title: The role of artificial intelligence in clinical trials: opportunities
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is now embedded across the clinical trial lifecycle, from target discovery and protocol design to recruitment, conduct, and post-marketing surveillance. Adoption has outpaced validation, and the randomised controlled trial (RCT) evidence base remains geographically uneven. For India, the question is no longer whether to adopt AI in trials, but how to do so without importing algorithms never validated on Indian patients. Narrative review of peer-reviewed literature (2018–2026) indexed in PubMed and major journal families, supplemented by official Indian regulatory documents (CDSCO, ICMR, MeitY). The review maps AI applications across the trial lifecycle, examines RCT evidence, and situates findings in India's regulatory context. A 2024 scoping review identified 86 AI RCTs (2018-2023); 81 per cent reported a positive primary endpoint, although 63 per cent were single-centre and only 19 per cent of post-2021 trials cited CONSORT-AI.1 Machine learning predicts early trial termination with area under the curve 0.80.2 The first generative-AI-discovered small molecule, rentosertib for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, completed phase 2a in 2025.3 Counter-examples persist: the Epic Sepsis Model showed sensitivity of 33 per cent on external validation.4 India's sepsis mortality (36.3 per cent overall; 50.8 per cent in septic shock) and projected antimicrobial-resistance deaths (11.8 million in South Asia by 2050) make trial-grade AI validation a national imperative. AI will reshape clinical trials, but only prospective, externally validated, reporting-standard-compliant studies, increasingly in Indian populations, will turn potential into evidence that regulators and clinicians can act on.

items.title: The Tawhidic Paradigm as Workplace Spirituality in Islamic Higher Education: Governance, Talent Management and Organizational Excellence
items.abstract: The concept of workplace spirituality is increasingly attracting scholarly attention due to its potential to foster meaningful work, ethical behavior, and organizational success. However, empirical research remains limited regarding how faith-based spirituality translates into formal organizational practices. This study explores the manifestation and institutionalization of the Tawhidic paradigm as a foundation for workplace spirituality within an Islamic higher education institution. Particular focus is placed on governance, talent management, and organizational excellence. Employing a qualitative case study approach, data were collected through semi-structured interviews and focus group discussions involving representatives from four staff associations and subsequently analyzed using thematic analysis. Three key themes emerged from the findings: the strength of spirituality and community spirit within the Tawhidic paradigm; challenges in governance and talent management; and the integration of workplace harmony with organizational excellence. The Tawhidic paradigm was found to provide a robust foundation for spirituality and community spirit. However, concerns regarding implementation transparency, recognition, career advancement, promotion criteria, and professional competence created a gap between held spiritual values ​​and formal organizational practices. This resulted in tension between harmony and excellence, suggesting that a supportive and comfortable work environment could contribute to complacency, resistance to change, and a lack of readiness to embrace technology and artificial intelligence (AI). By bridging the gap between values ​​and organizational practices, this study extends the scope of workplace spirituality beyond individual and communal experiences toward a more holistic framework for sustainable organizational excellence within Islamic higher education institutions.

items.title: The Tour Guide
items.abstract: A visitor to an unexplained ruin observes stones; the same visitor, accompanied by a competent guide, observes a civilisation. The difference between those two visits is not one of information but of interpretation – the conversion of fact into meaning – and it is the subject of this chapter. The chapter first establishes the guide's significance from three standpoints: that of the traveller, who engages a guide for reasons only marginally concerned with knowledge; that of the tour operator, for whom the guide is the sole part of the product the customer actually meets; and that of the destination, for whom the guide is its narrator to the world. It then sets out the theoretical foundations of guiding in Tilden's principles of interpretation and Cohen's analysis of the guide as both pathfinder and mentor , and examines the roles, types, competencies, working conditions and regulatory structures of the profession. Two contemporary developments are given particular attention: the rise of digital marketplaces, which have made the individual guide an entrepreneur and a brand while subjecting them to a new intermediary, and the challenge of artificial intelligence. On the latter the chapter offers no comfortable answer. The machine now explains monuments competently, and the profession's defence must rest instead on what the machine cannot do: it answers only questions the visitor has already thought to ask, it explains where a guide tells , it cannot feel or be felt, and it consumes the attention the traveller has crossed the world to spend.

items.title: The Travel Intermediaries
items.abstract: Since 1995 – the year in which the first airline capped agents’ commissions and the commercial internet arrived within a few months of each other – the travel intermediary has been repeatedly declared obsolete. Three decades later, it has not disappeared. This chapter explains why. It begins from the proposition that intermediaries exist not by custom but for reasons – they aggregate a fragmented supply, reduce the information asymmetry between traveller and supplier, lower the cost of transacting, absorb risk and provide someone to be answerable when a journey fails – and it argues that the fate of the intermediary depends entirely upon which of these functions a given technology can perform. The chapter traces the evolution of intermediation through four phases: the traditional agency founded by Thomas Cook; the disintermediation that the internet was expected to complete; the re-intermediation by which online travel agencies became more powerful than the intermediaries they replaced; and the present challenge from artificial intelligence, which the largest of those agencies now names as a competitor in its own annual report. The conclusion advanced is that disintermediation does not eliminate the intermediary; it relocates them – and that the functions technology cannot yet absorb, liability and recovery , are precisely the ones on which the traveller most depends when things go wrong.

items.title: The Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Islamic Religious Education: The Perceptions and Ethical Considerations of Islamic Religious Education Teachers in Lower Secondary Schools
items.abstract: The use of artificial intelligence (AI) in Islamic Religious Education (PAI) offers opportunities to develop a variety of teaching materials and strategies, but also presents challenges regarding the accuracy of information, academic integrity and the character development of pupils. This study aims to analyse PAI teachers’ perceptions of the use of AI, its practical application in teaching, and the associated ethical considerations at SMPN 5 Mesuji Raya. The study employs a qualitative approach using a case study design. Data were collected through interviews with one PAI teacher and one pupil. Data analysis followed the model proposed by Miles, Huberman and Saldaña, which includes data condensation, data presentation, and the drawing and verification of conclusions. The results indicate that AI is utilised to assist in the preparation of teaching modules, the creation of interactive quizzes, the development of visual media, and the design of case studies on moral values. The use of varied media is perceived to make learning more engaging. However, teachers’ acceptance of AI is critical and conditional, as the information generated requires verification and the technology cannot replace the teacher’s role as a role model, the shaping of moral character, or spiritual guidance. From an ethical perspective, the study highlights the importance of academic integrity and the application of the values of ṣidq (honesty) and tabayyun (verification of information) to guide the responsible use of AI. This study emphasises that the use of AI in Islamic Education must be accompanied by validation of the material, teacher support and clear rules of use to ensure it is aligned with learning objectives and Islamic values.

items.abstract: This commentary highlights the age illusion and advocates integrating biological age and artificial intelligence (AI) to enhance clinical precision in health care. By synthesizing geroscience and machine learning, practitioners and scientists can effectively bridge the gap between experimental biomarkers and personalized medicine and longevity care. This contribution is timely as the importance of biological age and predictive analytics offer transformative potential for diagnostics while necessitating a focus on modern medical systems. This article aims to elucidate how AI accelerates the clinical implementation of biological age rather than current chronological age in precision medicine.

items.title: Then there is prompt injection, a malicious email, ...: The Wild Wide West of OpenClaw Agentic System Security
items.abstract: AI-powered personal assistant frameworks such as OpenClaw combine LLM reasoning, persistent memory, tool invocation, local execution, and web-based workflows. These capabilities enable useful automation, but they also create security risks when untrusted inputs, model reasoning, tools, memory, and deployment configuration interact without explicit trust boundaries. This paper presents an empirical study of reported security concerns in OpenClaw using two complementary data sources: Reddit discussions and security-tagged GitHub issues. We analyze more than 25K Reddit posts from 13 OpenClaw-related subreddits and identify 162 security-relevant posts with 1,787 associated comments. We further collect 358 security-tagged GitHub issues and retain 180 issues describing concrete security concerns. Using qualitative analysis and evidence-grounded CWE mapping, we identify 521 CWE instances across 59 distinct weakness types, concentrated in access-control failures, sensitive-data exposure, injection, and unsafe execution. We also extract 543 practitioner mitigation suggestions and consolidate them into seven recurring strategies. To complement the empirical analysis, we present an evidence-grounded illustrative reconstruction of a representative sensitive-data exposure pathway using dummy secret values. Our findings show that OpenClaw security issues are not isolated implementation bugs; they reflect recurring trust-boundary failures across the agent execution pipeline. We discuss how these weaknesses map to both traditional software-security categories and agent-specific failure mechanisms, and derive implications for safer agentic systems, including explicit trust boundaries, least-privilege tool access, execution containment, runtime oversight, and defense-in-depth deployment.
